# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 11, 2026
**Re:** Gaimun Brewing Company, LLC / Breneth Systems, Inc.: BrewOps license package (issue-spotting review)
**Matter:** s42-m0001

---

## 1. Bottom Line

I reviewed all five documents in the folder:

- the Software License and Subscription Agreement dated November 2, 2026 (the "Agreement");
- Schedule B Service Level Schedule (the "SLS");
- the Side Letter dated November 2, 2026;
- Order Form No. 001; and
- the onboarding email thread of November 4–10, 2026.

I found **five significant issues** that we should resolve before Gaimun countersigns or relies further on the package. One of them is time-sensitive because of the pending Ostrander merger.

Two features of the documents drive most of the risk:

1. **The order of precedence clause (Agreement §1.4).** It ranks the documents in this order: Side Letter, then Order Form, then SLS, then the body of the Agreement. As a result, terms in the shorter ancillary documents override protections Gaimun negotiated in the main Agreement. This affects the data-loss remedy and the governing law.
2. **The 60-month term in the Order Form.** Combined with Agreement provisions that look routine on their own, it raises the dollar stakes considerably.

**Key commercial terms:**

| Term | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Agreement Effective Date | November 2, 2026 | Agreement, preamble |
| Subscription Start Date | January 1, 2027 | Order Form §2.1 |
| Initial Subscription Term | **60 months (five years)**, running through December 31, 2031 | Order Form §2.2 |
| Annual Subscription Fee | **$186,000 per year**, invoiced annually in advance | Order Form §3.1; Side Letter §1.1 |
| Total fees over the initial term | About $930,000 | Calculated |
| Monthly Fee (for service credits) | $15,500 (1/12 of the annual fee) | SLS §1.1(g) |
| General liability cap | Fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim (about $186,000) | Agreement §11.2 |
| Availability commitment | 99.5% per calendar month | SLS §2.1 |
| Ostrander merger agreement | Signed September 30, 2026; closing expected Q1 2027 | Side Letter Recital B |

**Summary of issues, in priority order:**

| # | Issue | Location | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ostrander merger triggers change-of-control consent; no consent obtained; fees can be accelerated | Agreement §14.2 (with Side Letter Recital B) | **Urgent: before closing** |
| 2 | Service credits made the sole remedy for data loss, overriding the uncapped data carve-out | SLS §5.4 (with Agreement §§1.4, 11.3(b)) | High |
| 3 | Side Letter moves governing law and forum to Colorado and Denver | Side Letter §4 (with Agreement §§1.4, 16.1–16.2) | High |
| 4 | Five-year automatic renewals with a 15-day opt-out window | Agreement §3.2 (with Order Form §2) | High |
| 5 | Breneth may assign freely, including to a competitor, without notice | Agreement §14.3 | Medium–High |

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: The Ostrander merger is a Change of Control requiring Breneth's consent, which has not been obtained

**Location:**
- Agreement §14.2, read with the Change of Control definition in §1.1(c) and with §14.1.
- The triggering facts appear in Side Letter Recital B.

**What the documents say:**

- **The definition is met.** "Change of Control" includes any merger "in which Customer becomes a subsidiary of another entity" (§1.1(c)(i)).
- **Consent is required.** Under §14.2, any Change of Control is "deemed an assignment" requiring Breneth's prior written consent under §14.1. Section 14.1 does not require Breneth to act reasonably, so Breneth may refuse for any reason.
- **The penalty is severe.** If a Change of Control occurs without consent, Breneth may terminate, and "all Fees for the remainder of the Subscription Term become immediately due and payable."
- **The merger is on the record.** Side Letter Recital B records that Gaimun signed a merger agreement on September 30, 2026 to become a wholly owned subsidiary of Ostrander Beverage Holdings LLC, with closing expected in Q1 2027. That is a squarely covered Change of Control.
- **No consent appears anywhere.**
  - The Side Letter deals only with pricing, onboarding, expansion pricing and governing law.
  - Side Letter §5.1 states: "Except as expressly set forth herein, the Agreement remains unchanged."
  - The Order Form says nothing about consent.
  - The email thread is purely operational and neither requests nor grants consent.

**Why it matters to Gaimun:**

- **The exposure is large.** If the merger closes without consent, Breneth can end the contract and demand the rest of the five-year fees at once, up to about $930,000 measured from the January 1, 2027 start date.
- **Gaimun would lose its operating system at the same moment.** The Platform runs batch records, TTB reporting, inventory and distributor ordering. Breneth's termination would cut Gaimun off from it in the middle of a merger integration.
- **Breneth's knowledge is probably not enough.** Breneth knew about the merger when it signed the Side Letter. However, Agreement §15.4 requires waivers and amendments to be in writing. I would not rely on an argument that Breneth's knowledge amounts to consent or a waiver.
- **Breneth gains negotiating leverage.** Breneth can use the consent requirement to extract concessions just before closing.

**Recommended fix (do this before countersignature, and in any event before closing):**

1. Obtain Breneth's express written consent to the Ostrander transaction, signed in accordance with §15.4. Ideally, add it to the Side Letter or a short amendment. The consent should confirm that the transaction will not trigger termination or acceleration under §14.2.
2. Also amend §14.2 going forward:
   - carve out transactions with Affiliates and internal reorganizations;
   - require that Breneth's consent not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed;
   - delete the fee-acceleration remedy, or at minimum limit Breneth's remedy to termination without acceleration.

**To confirm with the client:**
- the expected closing date;
- whether the merger agreement contains a covenant to obtain third-party consents, and whether the Breneth contract is (or should be) listed on the disclosure schedules;
- whether Ostrander's counsel knows about this contract.

**Open point on the acceleration amount:** The exact figure depends on timing. If the first annual invoice ($186,000) is paid in January 2027 and closing follows, the incremental exposure may be closer to $744,000. Breneth would likely argue for the full remaining balance. Also, "Subscription Term" is defined to include Renewal Terms (§1.1(q)). That increases the exposure if a renewal has already started when a later change of control occurs.

---

### Issue 2: The SLS makes capped service credits the "sole and exclusive remedy" for data loss, overriding the uncapped data-security carve-out

**Location:**
- SLS §5.4, read with SLS §5.3, Agreement §11.3(b) and Agreement §1.4.

**What the documents say:**

- **The Agreement removes the cap for data and confidentiality breaches.** Agreement §11.3(b) excludes from both the 12-month-fees cap (§11.2) and the exclusion of indirect damages (§11.1) any liability for breach of Section 8 (Data Security) or Section 9 (Confidentiality), "including liability for any loss or corruption of Customer Data and the costs of restoring it."
- **The SLS contradicts this.** SLS §5.4 states that Service Credits are Customer's "sole and exclusive remedy, and Breneth's sole liability, for any Service failure … including loss or corruption of Customer Data arising from or in connection with any Service failure."
- **The credits are tiny.** SLS §5.3 caps credits at 10% of the Monthly Fee. That is $1,550 per month.
- **The SLS wins a conflict.** Under Agreement §1.4, the SLS ranks above the body of the Agreement.
- **Nothing restores the carve-out.** Neither the Side Letter nor the Order Form addresses it.

**Why it matters to Gaimun:**

- **The data at risk is Gaimun's most sensitive.** Customer Data expressly includes Gaimun's recipes and formulations, batch records, production volumes, excise data and distributor pricing (§1.1(e)).
- **Breneth's likely argument is strong on the text.** If data is lost or corrupted during an outage or other "Service failure," Breneth will argue that Gaimun's only remedy is a credit of at most $1,550 for that month. That is far below even the general cap of about $186,000. The negotiated uncapped protection would effectively disappear for the scenarios where it matters most.
- **The ambiguity is not a reliable defense.** Gaimun could argue that §5.4 covers only data loss "arising from … any Service failure," while a breach of the Section 8 security obligations is a separate claim that remains uncapped. That argument is uncertain, and the "in connection with" wording is broad. We should not rely on it.

**Recommended fix:**

Revise SLS §5.4 as follows:

1. Delete the words "including loss or corruption of Customer Data."
2. Add express language stating that:
   - Service Credits are the sole remedy only for failure to meet the Availability Commitment and the response times; and
   - nothing in the SLS limits or excludes Breneth's liability under Agreement Sections 8, 9 or 11.3, or Gaimun's termination rights.

As a backstop, amend Agreement §1.4 so that §11.3 prevails over any conflicting provision in any Agreement Document.

---

### Issue 3: The Side Letter moves governing law and forum to Colorado and Denver for the entire Agreement

**Location:**
- Side Letter §4.1–4.2, read with Agreement §§16.1–16.2 and §1.4.

**What the documents say:**

- **The Agreement chooses New York.** Agreement §16.1 selects New York law. Agreement §16.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County.
- **The Side Letter chooses Colorado for everything.** Side Letter §4 provides that "this Side Letter and the Agreement as modified hereby" are governed by "the laws of the State of Colorado," with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in "Denver, Colorado."
- **The Side Letter wins a conflict.** Agreement §1.4 ranks the Side Letter first.
- **The clause is easy to miss.** The Side Letter is titled "Pricing Terms," and the governing law clause sits after the pricing provisions.

**Why it matters to Gaimun:**

- **Gaimun loses its negotiated home forum.** The provision effectively moves the entire license relationship to Breneth's home law and courts. This displaces the New York choice Gaimun negotiated.
- **Litigation would cost more.** Any dispute would have to be brought in Denver, which is costly and inconvenient for a Kingston brewery.
- **The clause would govern the key disputes.** That includes the change-of-control and data-loss issues above.
- **There are now two competing "exclusive" forum clauses.** That invites a threshold jurisdictional fight. It also creates a risk of arguments that the Side Letter and the Agreement are governed by different law.

**Recommended fix:**

- **Preferred:** Strike Side Letter §4 entirely.
- **Alternative:** Replace it with a sentence confirming that Agreement §§16.1–16.2 (New York law; New York County courts) govern the Side Letter and all Agreement Documents.
- **Either way:** Add to Agreement §1.4 that Section 16 controls over any conflicting provision in any other Agreement Document.

**To confirm with the client:** whether this term was discussed with Breneth or whether it is new. That will tell us how hard Breneth is likely to resist removing it.

---

### Issue 4: Automatic renewals for further five-year terms, with a 15-day opt-out window

**Location:**
- Agreement §3.2, read with Order Form §2.1–2.3 and Agreement §3.3.

**What the documents say:**

- **Renewals match the initial term.** Agreement §3.2 renews the subscription automatically for successive Renewal Terms "each equal in length to the Initial Subscription Term."
- **The notice window is narrow.** A non-renewal notice is effective only if delivered "no earlier than 60 days and no later than 45 days" before the end of the current term. A notice outside that window "shall not be effective."
- **The initial term is five years.** Order Form §2.2 sets the Initial Subscription Term at 60 months from January 1, 2027. Order Form §2.3 confirms renewal under §3.2.
- **The renewal terms are therefore also five years each, not one year.** The first term ends December 31, 2031. The only window to give notice of non-renewal runs from about **November 1 to November 16, 2031**.

**Why it matters to Gaimun:**

- **Each renewal is a large commitment.** If Gaimun misses that 15-day window by sending notice too early or too late, it is locked into another five-year term. At current pricing, that is about $930,000.
- **The fees cannot be escaped.** Fees are non-cancellable and non-refundable (§4.1). There is no right to terminate for convenience (§13).
- **The price hold ends after the initial term.** Renewal pricing is the final-year fee (§3.3). The Side Letter §1.1 price hold applies only to the Initial Subscription Term.
- **The lock-in is especially risky now.** Gaimun is growing and about to join Ostrander, which may want to consolidate onto its own systems.
- **The clause looks routine on its own.** The risk only appears when it is read with the Order Form.

**Recommended fix:**

- Limit Renewal Terms to 12 months or less.
- Replace the window with a simple deadline: notice is effective if given at least 90 days (or, at most, 60 days) before expiry, with no "no earlier than" limit.
- Optionally:
  - require Breneth to send a renewal reminder 30 days before the notice deadline;
  - cap any renewal-term price increase, for example at the CPI or a fixed percentage.

In the meantime, the client should calendar the November 1–16, 2031 window.

**To confirm with the client:** whether a five-year initial term was a deliberate commercial choice, for example in exchange for the price hold and the waived implementation fees. Also confirm whether Ostrander has a view on committing to a five-year platform.

---

### Issue 5: Breneth may assign the Agreement without consent or notice, including to a Gaimun competitor

**Location:**
- Agreement §14.3, contrasted with §14.1.

**What the documents say:**

- **Gaimun's assignment is restricted.** Gaimun may not assign without Breneth's prior written consent (§14.1).
- **Breneth's assignment is not.** Section 14.3 provides that Breneth "may assign this Agreement without Customer's consent" to any Affiliate, any successor by merger or reorganization, or any acquirer of "all or any part" of Breneth's business or assets.
- **There is no protection for Gaimun.** The clause has no notice requirement, no exclusion of competitors, and no termination right for Gaimun.

**Why it matters to Gaimun:**

- **Gaimun's data could end up with a rival.** Breneth could transfer the contract, and with it hosting of Gaimun's recipes, production volumes and distributor pricing, to a rival brewer or to a beverage conglomerate's software arm.
- **Gaimun would have no say and no warning.** It might not even learn of the transfer.
- **Contract protections may not be enough.** The confidentiality and security obligations would bind the assignee on paper. Even so, many breweries would see hosting by a competitor as unacceptable in practice.
- **The clause is one-sided.** "Any part of" the business allows piecemeal transfers to an entity that is less capable or less creditworthy than Breneth.

**Recommended fix:**

Make assignment mutual. Either party may assign to an Affiliate or to a successor of all or substantially all of its business, on these conditions:

- prior written notice of at least 30 days;
- the assignee assumes all obligations in writing;
- no assignment to a competitor of Gaimun (define "competitor" to include brewers and beverage producers and their affiliates) without Gaimun's consent;
- any other assignment requires consent not to be unreasonably withheld.

Add a right for Gaimun to terminate without penalty on assignment, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and full data export and deletion rights under §7.4.

Making the clause mutual also eases Issue 1 for future transactions.

---

## 3. Other Points (lower priority; for negotiation if there is room)

- **Expansion pricing may not cover Ostrander facilities.** Side Letter §3.2 gives a 15% discount only for facilities that Gaimun "owns or operates." After closing, facilities held by Ostrander or its other subsidiaries may not qualify. Given Recital B's anticipated growth, consider extending the discount to Affiliates.
- **No termination for convenience.** Combined with the non-refundable fees in §4.1, Gaimun has no exit short of a material breach by Breneth. Consider a termination right after year two, possibly with a modest fee.
- **Short data export window.** Under §7.4, Gaimun must request its data within 30 days after the Agreement ends. Consider 60–90 days, plus assistance with the transition.
- **No chronic-failure exit.** SLS §6.1 provides only a remediation meeting. Consider a right to terminate without penalty after repeated availability failures.

---

## 4. The Onboarding Email Thread

The thread (November 4–10, 2026) is operational. It does **not** modify any contract terms. It also says nothing about Breneth's consent to the Ostrander merger, so it does not affect Issue 1. Points worth noting:

- **It helps Gaimun on one point.** Jess Okafor's November 9 email expressly serves as Gaimun's written notice of its TTB filing deadlines under SLS §3.4. Breneth acknowledged it on November 10. This is useful and should be kept.
- **The descriptions match the documents.** The thread's description of support hours, maintenance windows and Severity 1 phone support is consistent with the SLS.
- **Data is already being shared.** Gaimun is uploading recipe and batch exports for migration before the package appears to be fully signed (see Section 5). If the Agreement is not yet in effect, the Section 8 and Section 9 protections may not clearly apply to those uploads.

---

## 5. Ambiguities and Items to Confirm with the Client

1. **Signing status.** All signature blocks in the folder copies are blank. Onboarding, however, is under way, and Breneth's email says "thanks again for choosing BrewOps." We need to confirm whether any document has been signed by either party.
   - If nothing is signed, we can negotiate these changes directly.
   - If anything is signed, each fix will need a written amendment signed by both parties under Agreement §15.4. Gaimun's leverage, especially on Issue 1, will be lower.
2. **Ostrander timing and merger agreement terms.** Confirm the expected closing date, any third-party-consent covenant or closing condition, and whether Ostrander intends to keep BrewOps. This affects both Issue 1 and Issue 4.
3. **History of the Side Letter §4 governing law clause.** Was it negotiated, or added by Breneth without discussion?
4. **The five-year commitment.** Was the 60-month term a deliberate trade for the price hold and the waived fees?
5. **Competitor sensitivities.** Does Gaimun know of any brewing or beverage companies with software affiliates that would make a Breneth assignment particularly concerning?
6. **Data already transferred.** Confirm what Customer Data has been uploaded and under what written terms, if any.

---

## 6. Suggested Next Steps

1. Confirm signing status and the Ostrander closing timeline with the client this week.
2. Send Breneth a short markup covering:
   - the written consent to the Ostrander transaction and revisions to §14.2 (Issue 1);
   - the SLS §5.4 carve-back and the §1.4 backstop (Issue 2);
   - deletion of Side Letter §4 (Issue 3);
   - the renewal-term and notice fix in §3.2 (Issue 4);
   - mutual assignment with a bar on assignment to competitors (Issue 5).
3. Advise the client not to countersign any document, and not to let the merger close, until Breneth's written consent is in hand.

I am happy to prepare the markup and a plain-language client summary once you have reviewed.

**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 11, 2026
**Re:** Gaimun Brewing Company, LLC / Breneth Systems, Inc. (BrewOps license package): issues and recommended pushback

---

## 1. Summary

I reviewed all five documents in the folder:

- the Software License and Subscription Agreement dated November 2, 2026 (the **Agreement**);
- Schedule B, the Service Level Schedule (the **SLS**);
- the Side Letter dated November 2, 2026;
- Order Form No. 001; and
- the onboarding email thread (November 4–10, 2026).

**Commercial basics**

- **Term:** a 60-month (five-year) Initial Subscription Term starting January 1, 2027 (Order Form §2.1–2.2).
- **Fee:** $186,000 per year, invoiced annually in advance (Order Form §3.1). The Side Letter §1.1 holds that fee fixed for the Initial Subscription Term.

**The precedence clause drives most of the risk.** Agreement §1.4 ranks the documents in this order: Side Letter, then Order Form, then SLS, then the Agreement body. As a result, protections Gaimun negotiated in the Agreement body are overridden by terms in the lower-profile documents.

**Four main issues, in rough priority order:**

1. **Governing law and forum (Side Letter §4).** The Side Letter moves the whole deal to Colorado law and Denver courts.
2. **Sole remedy for data loss (SLS §5.4).** The SLS reduces Gaimun's uncapped remedy for loss of its data (recipes, batch records, pricing) to small service credits.
3. **Automatic renewal (Agreement §3.2 with Order Form §2.2).** The deal renews automatically for further five-year terms, and the only way out is a 15-day notice window.
4. **Breneth's assignment right (Agreement §14.3).** Breneth can assign the contract to anyone, including a Gaimun competitor, without consent or notice.

I also note some smaller points and items to confirm with the client in Sections 3 and 4.

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: Side Letter moves the deal to Colorado law and Denver courts

**Location:** Side Letter §4.1–4.2. It conflicts with Agreement §16.1 (New York law) and §16.2 (exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts in New York County). Precedence is set by Agreement §1.4.

**What it says**
- Side Letter §4 applies to "this Side Letter and the Agreement as modified hereby."
- It chooses "the laws of the State of Colorado."
- It gives exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in "Denver, Colorado."

**Why it matters to Gaimun**
- The Side Letter is described as a pricing document, but §4 reaches the entire Agreement.
- Because §1.4 puts the Side Letter at the top of the order of precedence, Colorado law and a Denver forum would likely displace the New York choice Gaimun negotiated.
- Any dispute would be litigated on Breneth's home turf, under Breneth's home-state law, roughly 1,800 miles from Kingston.
- Even if Gaimun argued that §16 still controls, the documents now contain two competing "exclusive" forum clauses. That invites a costly fight over where to sue before the merits are ever reached.

**Recommended fix**
- Strike Side Letter §4 entirely. This is the preferred approach.
- Alternatively, replace it with a sentence confirming that Agreement §16.1–16.2 (New York law, New York County courts) governs the Side Letter and all Agreement Documents.
- Consider adding to Agreement §1.4 that §16 prevails over any conflicting term in another Agreement Document.

---

### Issue 2: SLS "sole and exclusive remedy" clause overrides the uncapped data-security carve-out

**Location:** SLS §5.4, read with SLS §5.3. It conflicts with Agreement §11.3(b). Precedence is set by Agreement §1.4.

**What it says**
- **The Agreement body protects Gaimun's data.**
  - Agreement §11.2 caps general liability at fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months.
  - Agreement §11.3(b) removes that cap for Breneth's breach of its data-security (§8) and confidentiality (§9) obligations, "including liability for any loss or corruption of Customer Data and the costs of restoring it."
  - Customer Data expressly includes recipes and formulations, batch records, production volumes and distributor pricing (Agreement §1.1(e)).
- **The SLS takes that protection away.**
  - SLS §5.4 makes Service Credits Gaimun's "sole and exclusive remedy" for any Service failure, "including loss or corruption of Customer Data arising from or in connection with any Service failure."
  - SLS §5.3 caps Service Credits at 10% of the Monthly Fee. At $186,000 per year, that is about $1,550 per month.

**Why it matters to Gaimun**
- Under §1.4, the SLS prevails over the Agreement body.
- If Breneth loses or corrupts Gaimun's recipe library or batch history, Breneth will argue that Gaimun's only remedy is a credit of at most about $1,550 for that month.
- That is far below the uncapped remedy in §11.3(b), and far below even the general 12-month cap of about $186,000.
- Recipes and formulations are among Gaimun's most valuable trade secrets. Batch records also underpin its TTB filings.
- Neither the Order Form nor the Side Letter restores the carve-out.
- **Ambiguity:** the phrase "arising from or in connection with any Service failure" is broad. Breneth could argue that almost any data-loss event (for example, a failed update or a backup failure) is a Service failure. We should not rely on a narrow reading.

**Recommended fix**
- Revise SLS §5.4 so that Service Credits are the sole remedy only for failures to meet the Availability Commitment and response times.
- Expressly exclude from §5.4 any loss or corruption of Customer Data, any Security Incident and any breach of Agreement §8 or §9.
- Add: "Nothing in this Schedule limits Breneth's liability under Section 11.3 of the Agreement."
- Consider amending §1.4 so that §11.3 prevails over any conflicting term in any Agreement Document.

---

### Issue 3: Automatic five-year renewals with a 15-day opt-out window

**Location:** Agreement §3.2, read with Order Form §2.2–2.3 and Agreement §3.3.

**What it says**
- Agreement §3.2 renews the subscription automatically for successive Renewal Terms, "each equal in length to the Initial Subscription Term."
- A non-renewal notice is effective only if delivered "no earlier than 60 days and no later than 45 days" before the end of the current term.
- A notice delivered outside that period "shall not be effective."
- The Order Form sets the Initial Subscription Term at 60 months from January 1, 2027.

**Why it matters to Gaimun**
- Read alone, §3.2 looks routine. Read with the Order Form, every renewal is another five years. It is not one year.
- At the current $186,000 annual fee, each renewal commits Gaimun to about $930,000.
- Under §3.3, renewal pricing carries over the final-year fee. The Side Letter price hold covers only the Initial Subscription Term.
- The first term ends December 31, 2031. The non-renewal window therefore runs roughly **November 1 to November 16, 2031**, a 15-day window.
- A notice sent too early is void, just like one sent too late. An early, careful notice would not protect Gaimun.
- **Ambiguity:** the exact window dates depend on how "days before the end" is counted, for example whether the last day of the term is included. Notice is effective "on receipt" under Agreement §15.1. The window should be confirmed and calendared conservatively.

**Recommended fix**
- Limit Renewal Terms to 12 months or less.
- Replace the 60/45-day window with a single deadline: notice of non-renewal at any time up to at least 90 days before expiry, with no "no earlier than" restriction.
- Ideally, require Breneth to send a renewal reminder 30 days before the notice deadline.
- Consider a cap on renewal-term price increases, for example CPI or a fixed percentage.
- Consider a termination-for-convenience right after the first 24–36 months, perhaps with a modest fee. That would give a growing business more flexibility.

---

### Issue 4: Breneth can assign freely, including to a competitor and without notice

**Location:** Agreement §14.3, contrasted with §14.1.

**What it says**
- Agreement §14.1 bars Gaimun from assigning without Breneth's prior written consent.
- Agreement §14.3 says Breneth "may assign this Agreement without Customer's consent" to any Affiliate, merger successor, or acquirer of "all or any part" of Breneth's business or assets.
- There is no notice requirement, no exclusion for competitors and no termination right for Gaimun.

**Why it matters to Gaimun**
- The clause is one-sided.
- Breneth could transfer the contract, and with it hosting of Gaimun's recipes, production volumes and distributor pricing, to the software arm of a large brewing company or another direct rival.
- Gaimun would have no say and might not even learn of the transfer until after the fact.
- The words "any part" of Breneth's business mean the contract could be split off to a smaller or less creditworthy buyer.
- The confidentiality obligations would technically follow the contract. Even so, the commercial and trust risk of a competitor holding Gaimun's core data is significant.

**Recommended fix**
- Make the assignment clause mutual. Each party may assign only with the other's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, with a carve-out for a sale of substantially all of the assigning party's business.
- Prohibit any assignment by Breneth to a Gaimun competitor, meaning any entity engaged in brewing or beverage production or distribution, or its affiliates.
- Require at least 30 days' prior written notice of any assignment.
- If Breneth assigns, give Gaimun a right to terminate without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
- Give Gaimun an extended data-export window and certified deletion on that termination.

---

## 3. Secondary points (lower priority)

- **Short data-export window (Agreement §7.4).** Gaimun must request export within 30 days after expiry or termination, after which Breneth deletes the data. Given that the batch history goes back to 2019 and supports TTB filings, I recommend 90 days and a right to request export at any time during the term.
- **Thin chronic-failure remedy (SLS §6.1).** Repeated outages trigger only a meeting and a remediation plan. I recommend a right to terminate without penalty, with a pro-rata refund, if Availability falls below 98.0% for two consecutive months or three months in any 12.
- **TTB reporting accuracy (Agreement §2.4, §10.2).** Gaimun bears full responsibility for filings. This is reasonable, but consider requiring Breneth to correct report-format errors promptly, and to treat a TTB-module failure near a filing deadline as Severity 1. The SLS §4.3 table already points this way.
- **Email thread (D5).** I found nothing in the thread that changes the legal terms. It is consistent with the documents: implementation fees waived, 25 users, Kingston site, maintenance windows and support channels. Jess Okafor's November 9 email serves as written notice of TTB filing deadlines under SLS §3.4. That appears adequate for that limited purpose, though it was sent to the implementation lead rather than the notice address in Agreement §15.1.

---

## 4. Items to confirm with the client

1. **Signature status.** The signature blocks in all four contract documents are blank, although they are dated November 2, 2026, and onboarding is already under way. Has Gaimun signed any of them? Our leverage depends on whether we are negotiating or amending.
2. **How the Side Letter §4 language arose.** Did Gaimun's team see and agree to the Colorado law and forum clause, or did it arrive in a "pricing only" document? This affects how we frame the pushback.
